sentences.text: Appearance:

Shri Dharmendra Dwivedi - Advocate for the legal represe
 of appellant(deceased).
Shri Kamal Kumar Rochalani- Advocate for respondent No.1

Order 
This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by LRs of deceased appellant, who is owner of the offending vehicle being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 08.05.2015 passed by 5th Additional MACT, Morena in Claims Case No.223/2015 seeking only liability on the Insurance Company to pay compensation amount to the claimants.
The date of accident, and negligence are not in dispute, however, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of deceased NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20280 2 MA-930-2015 Badri Singh due to motor accident, Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.4,37,200/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.

Shri Dwivedi, counsel submitted that at the time of accident, Driver of the offending vehicle was having a valid Insurance and, therefore, Claims Tribunal has committed an error in exonerating the Insurance Company from its liability.
It is further submitted that deceased -appellant took insurance from the Agent of the concerned Insurance Company and cover note was issued by him.

sentences.text: So, at the time of accident, he has a valid insurance.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.
Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.

After hearing counsel for the parties and on perusal of the entire record as well as impugned award,
it is found that owner of the offending vehicle is unable to produce any Insurance Policy or cover note as well as also unable to adduce evidence of the Agent, Shri Ashok Kumar, who made the cover note in favour of owner of the offending vehicle.

Therefore, due to lack of evidence, Claims Tribunal has rightly NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20280 3 MA-930-2015 exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability because at the time of accident, offending vehicle was not insured with Insurance Company.
So, this Court is of the considered opinion that Tribunal has rightly exonerated Insurance Company from its liability.
Hence, no interference is required of this Court.
Accordingly, the appeal being devoid of merit is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *AVI*
